A [[Raleigh, North Carolina]], native, Wall was chosen with the [[List of first overall NBA draft picks|first overall pick]] of the [[2010 NBA draft]] by the Wizards after playing one year of [[college basketball]] for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]]. Wall, who played the [[point guard]] position, was a five-time [[NBA All-Star]] from 2014 to 2018 and was named to the [[All-NBA Team]] in 2017. However, he experienced multiple injuries in 2019 and missed more than two years of basketball before being traded to the [[Houston Rockets]] in December 2020. After two seasons with the Rockets, he joined the Clippers via free agency before being dealt back to the Rockets, with which he reached a buyout in February 2023. ==Early life== Wall was born on September 6, 1990, to Frances Pulley and John Carroll Wall Sr. When he was a year old, his father, who had previously served time in prison for second-degree murder, was convicted of armed robbery. After his second season, his family moved to [[Raleigh]]. He attended [[Broughton High School (North Carolina)|Broughton High School]], where he repeated his sophomore year. Despite having a very impressive tryout, Wall was cut from the school's varsity team for attitude-related issues.(January 3, 2017). [https://slamonline.com/nba/john-wall-reflects-hs-days/ John Wall Reflects On Getting Cut From HS Team, Talks Kentucky Hoops]. ''slamonline.com''. Retrieved May 23, 2026.(October 31, 2012). [https://www.highschoolot.com/story/raleigh-s-john-wall-thankful-for-hometown-support/11723072/ Raleigh's John Wall thankful for hometown support]. ''highschoolot.com''. Retrieved May 23, 2026. For this reason, he transferred to [[Word of God Christian Academy]], also in Raleigh. It was there that Wall set about the reform of his attitude and related issues. Coach Levi Beckwith worked with Wall, first to stop demeaning his teammates for missed layups, and later to improve his facial expressions and general demeanor. On the heels of his second sophomore year of high school, in the summer of 2007, Wall was invited to the prestigious Reebok All-American Camp in Philadelphia; there, he distinguished himself by scoring 28 points against a team that featured future lottery pick [[Brandon Jennings]]. In 2008, Wall played in the Elite 24 Hoops Classic, at which he scored 10 points and won co-MVP honors alongside Dominic Cheek, [[Maalik Wayns]], and [[Lance Stephenson]].{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/elite-24-hoops-classic.shtml|title=2008 ELITE 24 BASKETBALL GAME RESULTS|date=August 22, 2008|publisher=InsideHoops.com|access-date=September 30, 2010}} As a fifth-year senior in 2009, Wall averaged 19.7 points, nine assists, and over eight rebounds for [[Word of God Christian Academy]]{{cite web|url=http://www.maxpreps.com/news/RtIjDkTqEd6pcwAcxJTdpg/kentucky-lands-star-pg-wall.htm|title=Kentucky Lands Star PG Wall|last=Krider|first=Dave|date=May 19, 2009|publisher=MAXPREPS.com|access-date=September 30, 2010}} and was ranked one of the best high school basketball players in the class of that year.{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/recruiting/rankings/rank-1642|title=Rivals.com Ranking – Rivals150 for class of 2009|date=April 16, 2009|publisher=Yahoo! He finished with 19 points, two rebounds, five assists, and three steals. On December 29, 2009, against Hartford, Wall set the Kentucky single-game assist record with 16, 11 in the first half, with only one turnover. The mark was previously held by [[Travis Ford]], at 15, and was broken on Ford's 40th birthday. Wall scored nine points, failing to break double digits for the first time in his college career. Over the course of the [[2009–10_NCAA_Division_I_men%27s_basketball_season|2009-2010 season]], Wall led the [[2009–10_Kentucky_Wildcats_men%27s_basketball_team|Wildcats]] in scoring, assists, and steals en route to a SEC regular season and SEC tournament championship, a 29-2 regular season record, and an Elite Eight tournament appearance. On September 22, 2017, Wall was inducted into the University of Kentucky Athletics Hall of Fame.{{Cite news|url=http://ftw.usatoday.com/2017/09/john-wall-cry-tears-mom-thank-you-kentucky-hall-of-fame-speech-heartfelt-video|title=John Wall fights back tears while thanking his mom in Kentucky Hall of Fame speech|date=September 23, 2017|work=For The Win|access-date=September 26, 2017|language=en-US}} ==Professional career== Because Wall was a [[Super senior|fifth-year high school senior]] in 2009 and would turn 19 by the end of the year, some sources argued that he would be eligible for the [[2009 NBA draft]]. League rules stated that American players must turn 19 during the year of the draft and be a year removed from their regular high school class. NBA spokesman Tim Frank told sportswriter [[Chad Ford]] that the league was not sure whether Wall met the second criterion, and that league officials would need to "do [their] due diligence to determine his eligibility".{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2009/columns/story?columnist=ford_chad&page=DraftWatch-090414|title=Buzz from the Nike Hoop surgery] ==Player profile== [[File:John Wall (Clippers at Wizards 12-18-16).jpg|thumb|Wall celebrates victory in 2016]] Wall is known for being one of the NBA's fastest players. His results at the draft combine of 10.84 seconds in the lane agility drill (combine best that year) and 3.14 seconds in the 3/4 court sprint (second-best that year) demonstrated his horizontal and vertical quickness. Despite only being a point guard-average {{convert|6|ft|4|in|m|2}} listed height in shoes and {{convert|6|ft|2.75|in|m|2}} barefoot, Wall has a {{convert|6|ft|9.25|in|m|2}} wingspan, slightly larger than the average for a point guard.{{Cite news|url=https://fansided.com/pg-wing-2016/|title=pg wing 2016|date=June 23, 2016|work=FanSided|access-date=December 9, 2017}}[http://www.nbadraft.net/nba-draft-combine-athleticism-test-results NBA Draft Combine: Athleticism Test Results] Relying on his speed, Wall focuses on driving to the basket and sparking fast transition play.{{Cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/wizards/john-wall-injury-could-cost-wizards-vs-hawks/2015/05/05/4f3a81d6-f394-11e4-bcc4-e8141e5eb0c9_story.html|title=Without Wall, Wizards' hands are tied|last=Lee|first=Michael|date=May 6, 2015|newspaper=Washington Post|access-date=January 19, 2017}} He is also a skilled passer, averaging over 10 assists a game for the 2014 through 2017 seasons, and 9.2 overall for his career.{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/w/walljo01.html|title=John Wall Stats {{!}} Basketball-Reference.com|website=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=December 9, 2017}} In the earlier stages of his time in the NBA, Wall was criticized for the amount of turnovers he committed, being dubbed "very turnover prone".[http://www.nbadraft.net/players/john-wall 11 – John Wall] While increasing his assist to turnover ratio in later years, Wall's TOPG has increased to 4.1, his mark at the conclusion of the 2017 season. Despite Wall's shooting percentages hovering slightly below league average except for [[free throw]] shooting (League average is .458/.364/.765 while Wall shoots .433/.321/.790{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/leagues/NBA_stats.html|title=NBA League Averages {{!}} Basketball-Reference.com|website=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=December 9, 2017}}), he has seen his shooting largely improve throughout his NBA career. John Wall is ambidextrous even though he shoots right-handed. He signed another five-year deal with Adidas in 2018.{{cite news |last1=Allen |first1=Scott |date=January 7, 2018 |title=Two years after John Wall and Adidas parted ways, they've struck a new deal |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/dc-sports-bog/wp/2018/01/07/two-years-after-john-wall-and-adidas-parted-ways-theyve-reportedly-struck-a-new-deal/ |access-date=February 2, 2019 |newspaper=Washington Post}} In May 2017, Wall signed on as a brand ambassador for New Era caps.{{Cite news |date=May 26, 2017 |title=Wizards' John Wall lands new endorsement deal on heels of career-best season |url=http://www.nbcsports.com/washington/washington-wizards/wizards-john-wall-lands-new-endorsement-deal-heels-career-best-season |access-date=December 25, 2017 |work=NBC Sports Washington}} In 2013, after signing a five-year contract with the Washington Wizards, Wall purchased a home in [[Potomac, Maryland|Potomac]] for $4.9 million.
